extracted.intended_audience: Depositors (researchers, patent applicants/agents) seeking to deposit biological material (microorganisms, plasmids, cell lines, seeds etc.) with culture collections under the Budapest Treaty
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and acceptance/administrative requirements for depositing biological material (microorganisms, plasmids, cell lines, seeds, viruses, etc.) with national culture collections for patent purposes under the Budapest Treaty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kinds of Microorganisms that May Be Deposited (CChRGM - Chile)
rubrics_metrics.description: CChRGM may receive for long-term deposit microorganisms for agricultural and forestry, environmental and industrial-process use and impact. More specifically, CChRGM will accept for deposit fungi (molds, filamentous fungi, yeasts, higher fungi), bacteria (including actinomycetes), microorganisms which contain plasmids; those which can be preserved, without any alteration to their properties, by means of sub-culture and storage in cryopreservation and lyophylization. CChRGM will accept pathogenic microorganisms from plants, antagonists of phytopathogens, nematophogae, entomopathogens, mycorrhizal, plant endophytes, bioremediators and microorganisms from industrial processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preparations of nucleic acids and phages are not accepted for the time being. Algae, protozoa, human cell lines, animal viruses and hybridomas cannot be received at present. Only strains that may be cultivated and preserved under technically feasible conditions for the collection, without inducing significant changes in characteristics, can be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions and Right to Refuse (CChRGM - Chile)
rubrics_metrics.description: Animal and human pathogenic microorganisms and/or of unknown nature are excluded from being deposited as such. Mixtures of cultures, contaminated cultures, those without an adequate scientific description or cultures whose identity cannot be verified are excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curator reserves the right to accept or reject microorganisms which require special treatment or present a handling/storage risk; exceptional acceptance may be negotiated case-by-case including costs and conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and Quantity Requirements (CChRGM - Chile)
rubrics_metrics.description: Organisms must be submitted for deposit as liquid cultures or in agar. Lyophilized samples will be accepted only after rehydration and positive culturing. Minimum number of replicas must be supplied (example: in the case of fungi, a pure culture in a known culture medium, free of contamination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contaminated cultures will be rejected without processing. International shipping/packaging rules implied; specifics determined case-by-case by curator when special treatment required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viability Testing Timeframe (CChRGM - Chile)
rubrics_metrics.description: The average time required to carry out the viability analysis by CChRGM is 15 days, but depositors must take into account that in some cases analysis may take up to 30 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any change in testing time will be notified to the depositor in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositor Checks and Renewal of Stocks (CChRGM - Chile)
rubrics_metrics.description: CChRGM will prepare its own sub-cultures of organisms at the time of deposit. Cultures will be renewed in accordance with requests or the opinion of the laboratory already established for the different groups of microorganisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where original material was cryopreserved, renewal is by subculture or by requesting a new deposit from the depositor. Analysis of authenticity of the samples is required from the first group of samples for deposit (not from subsequent ones).

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Requirements: Language and Contract (CChRGM - Chile)
rubrics_metrics.description: Official languages of CChRGM are Spanish and English. Depositor must complete the application form (serves as contract) whereby the depositor undertakes to supply all requested information, pay required fees, compensate CChRGM for claims from altered/misleading/third-party information, decline to withdraw deposit during the required storage period, and authorize CChRGM to supply samples in accordance with Rule 11 of the Regulations under the Budapest Treaty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where an organism has been accepted for deposit, CChRGM shall notify the depositor and remind him of the contract terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Import/Quarantine Compliance (CChRGM - Chile)
rubrics_metrics.description: Type of organisms accepted is subject to import and/or quarantine regulations and internationally recognized biosafety protocols. For import and quarantine purposes, depositors must follow requirements and regulations of the Livestock and Agriculture Service (Servicio Agricola Ganadero) and national customs services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositors from abroad must be aware of their country’s import requirements for receipt of furnished samples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making an Original Deposit and Use of International BP Forms (CChRGM - Chile)
rubrics_metrics.description: Depositors must complete the application and deposit forms used by CChRGM for deposits according to the Budapest Treaty, equivalent to BP/1. Receipt and declaration of viability are issued on international forms BP/4 and BP/9 respectively. Certificates for later indication or amendment of scientific description/taxonomic designation on BP/8; notification of supply to third parties on BP/14.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unofficial provisional notifications (date of deposit, entry number) may be communicated by telephone/fax/email before official receipt is issued, but are provisional pending viability testing. CChRGM will supply copies of receipt and viability statement to depositor’s patent agent if requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Converting Previous Deposits (CChRGM - Chile)
rubrics_metrics.description: CChRGM does not hold deposits made for patent purposes beyond what is stipulated by the Budapest Treaty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No further conversion details provided; contact curator for case-by-case guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making a New Deposit (CChRGM - Chile)
rubrics_metrics.description: When making a new deposit the depositor shall be asked to complete model form BP/2 and attach documents required under Rule 6.2. Receipt and viability certificate for a new deposit are issued using international forms BP/5 and BP/9.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the documentation checklist of Rule 6.2 when submitting a new deposit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Furnishing of Samples: Requests, Notification, Cataloguing (CChRGM - Chile)
rubrics_metrics.description: CChRGM will inform third parties of correct procedures for valid requests and supply request forms used by industrial property offices or copies of BP/12 if proof of authorization required. Depositor will be informed by letter and email where samples have been sent. Deposits are catalogued/published only with written authorization of the depositor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For foreign requests, CChRGM assumes the depositor knows their own import requirements. Samples come from groups of specific preparations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule of Fees (CChRGM - Chile)
rubrics_metrics.description: Storage of each strain: 435,000 CLP (30 years). Issue of viability report: 45,000 CLP. Supply of a sample: 60,000 CLP. Communication of information: 15,000 CLP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amounts do not include dispatch costs and additional costs within Chile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for Depositors (CChRGM - Chile)
rubrics_metrics.description: CChRGM does not at present produce specific written notes for prospective depositors but is ready to give advice by telephone, letter or email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact curator directly for informal guidance prior to deposit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kinds of Microorganisms that May Be Deposited (CCTCC - China)
rubrics_metrics.description: CCTCC generally accepts algae, animal viruses, animal cell cultures, bacteria, bacteriophages, eukaryotic DNA, fungi, human cell cultures, stem cells, hybridomas, molds, mycoplasma, nematodes, oncogenes, plant cell cultures and plant seeds, plant viruses, plasmids, protozoa (non-parasitic) and yeasts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the microorganism is a dangerous pathogen the depositor should consult CCTCC in advance. CCTCC does not accept pathogenic microorganisms of Risk Group 1 & 2 (Chinese classification). It also does not accept biological material restricted from import according to Chinese law or whose conservation involves excessive hazards; rejects applications asking CCTCC to supply material restricted from export. Currently does not accept embryos, parasitic and pathogenic protozoa and RNA preparations. Director reserves right to reject material representing an unacceptable risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and Quantity Requirements (CCTCC - China)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bacteria, molds, yeasts, algae and viruses must be submitted as lyophilized preparations (agar stab/slant also acceptable). Viruses that cannot be lyophilized should be frozen. Plasmids or other vectors as isolated DNA must be furnished freeze-dried or precipitated in alcohol. All kinds of viruses and plasmids need to be sent together with a suitable host if the host is not available in the public collection. Material must be free from contamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All replicates should be from the same batch. A minimum number of replicates table is provided by CCTCC (examples in the table include bacteriophages 5 x 0.5 ml free-cell lysate, plasmids DNA at least 20 meg/tube, seeds in the thousands). Consult CCTCC table for specific minima by material type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viability Testing Timeframes (CCTCC - China)
rubrics_metrics.description: Average testing times by type (CCTCC): Bacteria: 3 days (or up to 14 days). Algae, molds, yeasts: 5 days (or up to 20 days). Animal cell lines, hybridomas, bacteriophages, plasmids: 7 days (or up to 14 days). Animal viruses, plant cell cultures, seeds: 21 days (or up to 30 days). Plant viruses: no period yet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositors should realize testing may take longer in some cases; CCTCC will notify provisional results when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositor Checks and Renewal of Stocks (CCTCC - China)
rubrics_metrics.description: CCTCC prepares its own depositing batches in lyophilized or frozen form from original material supplied by the depositor. Deposits could also be made by subculturing at the depositor's request. CCTCC generally does not prepare its own batches of animal and plant viruses, plasmids, seeds, and some animal cell lines, hybridomas and plant tissue cultures. When stocks are depleted by furnishing samples, CCTCC will ask the depositor to make a new deposit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositors may be asked to provide new material for categories CCTCC cannot batch-produce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Requirements: Language and Contract (CCTCC - China)
rubrics_metrics.description: Working languages are Chinese and English. Depositors must complete application and accession form BP/1. CCTCC does not enter into a written contract defining liabilities except for certain dangerous organisms where depositor must accept and handle at own risk. By signing deposit forms and paying fees depositor surrenders right to withdraw deposit during required storage period and recognizes distribution according to the Budapest Treaty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositor must supply necessary information requested by CCTCC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Import and Quarantine Procedures (CCTCC - China)
rubrics_metrics.description: Overseas depositors must contact CCTCC in advance for shipping advice. Microorganisms are subject to Chinese import/quarantine regulations. The prospective depositor must supply the species name so CCTCC can apply for import license/quarantine; obtaining permit usually takes one or two weeks. CCTCC will inform depositor or patent agent when import permit obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositor must follow CCTCC instructions; import permits/clearances handled by CCTCC with local authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making Original/New Deposits and International Forms (CCTCC - China)
rubrics_metrics.description: Depositors are required to complete model form BP/1 for original deposits. Later indication/amendment use BP/7; receipt and viability statements are issued on BP/4 and BP/9 respectively; attestation of receiving later information on BP/8; notification of furnishing on BP/14. For new deposits complete BP/2 and supply Rule 6.2 documents; receipt and viability for new deposit issued on BP/5 and BP/9.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unofficial notifications (date and accession number) may be given by telephone/fax before official receipt but are provisional pending positive viability test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Converting Previous Deposits (CCTCC - China)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deposits made outside the Budapest Treaty may be converted by the original depositor to Budapest Treaty deposits; any deposits previously made free of charge are subject upon conversion to the storage fee normally levied. Administrative requirements for conversion are the same as for an original deposit, except import/quarantine procedures do not apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact CCTCC to arrange conversion and pay applicable fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Furnishing Samples: Requests, Withholding for Permits, Cataloguing (CCTCC - China)
rubrics_metrics.description: CCTCC advises third parties about correct procedures and provides BP/12 or national request forms. CCTCC will withhold samples subject to health and safety regulations until requester shows a permit to work with such organisms. For overseas requests CCTCC must obtain an export permit and assumes requester has met import requirements. Except for animal viruses, plasmids, seeds, and some cell lines/hybridomas/plant tissue cultures, furnished samples are from CCTCC's own preparations. Depositors are notified on BP/14 when samples are furnished. CCTCC lists deposits in its catalogue when depositor gives written authorization; all microorganisms subject of granted and published Chinese patents are listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requesters must show entitlement and necessary permits; depositors may control catalogue listing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule of Fees (CCTCC - China)
rubrics_metrics.description: Storage: RMB 3,000. Issuance of a viability statement: RMB 500. Furnishing of a sample: RMB 500. Communication of information: RMB 200. Application for import/export license: depends on individual situation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other currencies converted to RMB at Bank of China exchange rate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for Depositors (CCTCC - China)
rubrics_metrics.description: CCTCC has published a leaflet describing its activities available to possible depositors. Detailed information is available by email, telephone, telefax, or letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the leaflet or contact CCTCC for specifics before deposit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kinds of Microorganisms that May Be Deposited (CGMCC - China General)
rubrics_metrics.description: With the exception of pathogenic microorganisms of Risk Group 1 (Chinese classification): bacteria (including actinomycetes), yeasts, filamentous fungi, anaerobic microorganisms, single cell algae, animal cell lines, plant cell lines, mycoplasma, viruses, bacteriophages, plasmids, plant seeds are accepted. Protozoa not accepted temporarily.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a general rule CGMCC accepts strains that can be placed in culture under technically feasible conditions and conserved without inducing significant changes. Exceptionally, deposits requiring active culture may be accepted case-by-case with negotiated fees/conditions. CGMCC reserves right to refuse material restricted from import or whose conservation involves excessive hazards, and to refuse requests for materials restricted from export.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and Minimum Replicates Required (CGMCC - China General)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cultures are accepted in any form. Minimum number of replicates: Bacteria, yeasts, filamentous fungi, phages, mycoplasma, single cell algae: 5. Viruses, plasmids (not cloned into a host), animal cell lines, plant cell lines: 15. Plant seeds: 2,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CGMCC prepares lyophilized/frozen batches at deposit time for many categories. For plasmids 'viability' testing consists of inserting plasmid into a host; transformation indicates positive test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viability Testing Timeframes (CGMCC - China General)
rubrics_metrics.description: Average testing times: Bacteria, yeasts: 3 days (or up to 20 days). Filamentous fungi, mycoplasma: 6 days (or up to 30 days). Phages, single cell algae, animal cell lines: 7 days (or up to 14 days). Plasmids: 8 days (or up to 14 days). Animal viruses, plant cell lines, plant seeds: 21 days (or up to 30 days). Plant viruses: no date as yet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositors should note the maximum ranges for slow-growing or difficult-to-test materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositor Checks, Authenticity, and Renewal (CGMCC - China General)
rubrics_metrics.description: CGMCC prepares its own lyophilized/frozen batches for bacteria, actinomycetes, yeasts, filamentous fungi, phages, single cell algae and in some cases viruses by subculture or directly from active material supplied. New batches are prepared as necessary for renewal. CGMCC stores/distributes lyophilized material supplied by the depositor if desired. Generally does not prepare own batches of animal viruses and plasmids; when stocks depleted it will ask the depositor for a new deposit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CGMCC requires depositor to check authenticity of its lyophilized preparations and record results on the viability statement; if depositor does not inform CGMCC within three months, CGMCC assumes equivalence to depositor's original deposit. CGMCC stores a portion of original prepared material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Requirements: Language, Contract and Fees (CGMCC - China General)
rubrics_metrics.description: Working languages are Chinese and English. CGMCC does not enter into written contract except for certain dangerous organisms (depositor accepts/handles at own risk). By completing CGMCC BP/1 the depositor surrenders right to withdraw during required storage period and authorizes CGMCC to supply samples as required by patent procedure. Depositors must pay necessary fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Import permit for foreign deposits typically takes about seven days (or up to 14); depositors must pay for quarantine. CGMCC will inform depositor/patent agent when permit obtained. Unofficial notifications (date/accession) may be provided for a fee (e.g., $10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Making Original/New Deposits and International Forms (CGMCC - China General)
rubrics_metrics.description: Depositors are required to complete CGMCC form BP/1. Official notifications: receipt and viability statements issued on BP/4 and BP/9; notification of release to third party on BP/14. For new deposits CGMCC may accept under Article 4 and Rule 6.2; depositor asked to supply acknowledgement that new deposit is same as original and copies of relevant documents. Standard forms not required in some cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CGMCC will supply copies of receipt and viability statements to depositor's patent agent if requested. A fee may be charged for unofficial early notification services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Furnishing of Samples: Eligibility, Withholding and Cataloguing (CGMCC - China General)
rubrics_metrics.description: CGMCC will furnish samples to interested industrial property offices, depositor or authorized parties and parties legally entitled under Rule 11.3. It advises third parties on correct request procedures and provides BP/12 when proof of entitlement required. CGMCC withholds samples subject to health and safety regulations until it confirms requester can comply. Some organisms may require a permit from Chinese departments before release. Except for animal viruses and plasmids, CGMCC furnishes samples of its own preparations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When instructed by depositor or competent patent office to make samples available to anyone, the organism is listed in next published CGMCC catalog. All microorganisms subject of granted and published Chinese patents are listed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule of Fees (CGMCC - China General)
rubrics_metrics.description: Storage: USD 800. Issuance of a viability statement: USD 100. Furnishing of a sample: USD 100. Communication of information: USD 50.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other currencies will be converted into US dollars according to Bank of China exchange rate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for Depositors (CGMCC - China General)
rubrics_metrics.description: CGMCC publishes a brochure giving details of its requirements and practices for the deposit of cultures for patent purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prospective depositors should consult the brochure or contact CGMCC for detailed instructions prior to deposit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kinds of Microorganisms that May Be Deposited (CCM - Czech Republic)
rubrics_metrics.description: CCM accepts bacteria (including actinomycetes), filamentous fungi, yeast-like microorganisms and yeasts capable of long-term preservation without substantial change. Plasmids in a host are accepted (only plasmids belonging to group P1). CCM accepts only bacteria and fungi in hazard groups I or II per WHO Laboratory Biosafety Manual (1983).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Microorganisms with special cultivation requirements that CCM cannot carry out shall not be accepted. Cultures lacking scientific description or that cannot be identified will not be accepted. For plasmid-containing strains CCM requires information on plasmid and host properties and classification (group P1-P4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and Minimum Replicates Required (CCM - Czech Republic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bacteria and fungi, including those containing plasmids, are accepted as lyophilized or actively growing cultures (agar plate cultures not accepted). The depositor is required to provide two lyophilized or agar cultures when making a deposit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agar plate cultures are prone to damage in transport and thus not preferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viability Testing Timeframe (CCM - Czech Republic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Average time required for viability testing is five days, but for slow growing microorganisms viability testing may take as long as 14 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositors should allow additional time for slow-growing strains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositor Checks, Renewal and Authenticity (CCM - Czech Republic)
rubrics_metrics.description: CCM prepares its own lyophilized and/or frozen batches of bacteria and fungi at time of deposit by subculturing material supplied by the depositor. New batches are prepared as necessary for renewal when stocks diminish. The depositor is required to test for authenticity samples from all batches prepared by CCM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CCM keeps original material supplied by the depositor regardless of the batch preparation method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Requirements: Language, Forms and Notifications (CCM - Czech Republic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Official language is Czech; communications in English are also accepted. Depositors are required to complete form CCM-BP/1 (equivalent to BP/1). Receipt and viability statements are issued on BP/4 and BP/9 (both in Czech and English). Notification of furnishing to third party issued on BP/14. CCM uses its own standard letters for other official notifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requested, CCM will telephone/fax date of deposit and accession number before official receipt is issued, but only after a positive viability test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Converting Previous Deposits and Making New Deposits (CCM - Czech Republic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deposits made outside the Budapest Treaty may be converted to Treaty deposits only if they were originally made for patent purposes. Administrative requirements for conversion are similar to those for an original deposit; conversions are subject to the storage fee normally levied. For a new deposit the depositor must complete the equivalent of BP/2 and supply copies of documents required by Rule 6.2; receipts/viability for new deposit issued on BP/5 and BP/9.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact CCM for procedure and fees when converting previous deposits or making a new deposit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Furnishing of Samples and Cataloguing (CCM - Czech Republic)
rubrics_metrics.description: CCM advises third parties on correct procedures for valid requests and provides BP/12 where proof of entitlement is needed. When responding to overseas requests CCM may ask requester to provide an import permit if known to be required. All samples furnished by CCM are from batches of its own preparations. Depositors are notified on BP/14 when samples have been furnished. CCM does not list Budapest Treaty deposits in its published catalog.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositor may waive notification rights; otherwise BP/14 notifications are standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule of Fees (CCM - Czech Republic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent deposit of cultures (30 years): deposit and storage CZK 23,000; issuance of a viability statement CZK 700; furnishing of a sample CZK 1,000. VAT and extra charges for handling, postage and banking may apply; prepayment may be requested for foreign orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm current fees and additional charges with CCM prior to deposit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for Depositors (CCM - Czech Republic)
rubrics_metrics.description: CCM does not have specific written notes for depositors at present but is ready to offer advice by telephone or correspondence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact CCM staff for informal guidance and clarification of requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kinds of Microorganisms that May Be Deposited (VTTCC - Finland)
rubrics_metrics.description: VTTCC accepts bacteria (including actinomycetes) and fungi (including yeasts) which can be preserved at -150°C or in freeze-dried state without significant damage to or loss of properties or viability. VTTCC accepts only organisms belonging to risk groups 1 or 2 according to Directive 2000/54/EC and genetically modified microorganisms belonging to class 1 according to Council Directive 98/81/EC on the contained use of GM microorganisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Biological material contaminated by foreign organisms cannot be accepted. Mixtures of more than two microorganisms will not be accepted; mixtures of two may be accepted only if they cannot be cultivated separately and can be easily distinguished macroscopically or microscopically. VTTCC reserves right to refuse material representing unacceptable hazard or which it cannot process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and Quantity Requirements (VTTCC - Finland)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bacteria, yeasts and filamentous fungi submitted for deposit should be supplied as three active or freeze-dried cultures of the same batch. Cultures submitted should be free of foreign organisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International regulations for packaging and shipping of microorganisms should be followed in the consignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viability Testing Timeframe (VTTCC - Finland)
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimum time required for viability testing of kinds of microorganisms accepted by VTTCC is 7 days. Depositors should consider that viability testing of slow growing organisms and organisms with special growth requirements may take longer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow additional time for slow growers or organisms with special culture requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositor Checks and Renewal of Stocks (VTTCC - Finland)
rubrics_metrics.description: VTTCC will prepare its own subcultures and renew stocks as necessary; (detailed procedures continue beyond chunk).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact VTTCC for specific renewal schedules and depositor authentication checks.
